contentBlocks.text: Common Reasons for SASSA Grant Decline & How to Appeal Them
SASSA declines grants for specific coded reasons. Knowing exactly why you were declined helps you file a targeted appeal with the right evidence.
This guide is for SASSA applicants who want to understand why their grant was declined and what kind of evidence they need to submit for a successful appeal.

steps.title: Check your decline notification
steps.description: Check your decline notification for the specific reason code or description.

steps.title: Select your reason
steps.description: Select the matching reason from the ITSAA appeal dropdown menu.

steps.title: Upload evidence
steps.description: Upload evidence that directly addresses the decline reason.

steps.title: Wait for ruling
steps.description: Wait for the tribunal to review your appeal against the evidence.

rows: Your ID is linked to a UIF record
Submit a UI-19 termination letter from Department of Labour
Your ID is in the NSFAS database
Submit bank statements showing no income + sworn affidavit
Submit updated financial records showing lower income
Visit Home Affairs to correct your details
Ensure the account is in your name and active
File an appeal explaining your actual situation

faqs.question: Can I appeal if I do not know the reason for decline?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select 'Other' as the reason and explain your situation. The tribunal will investigate the underlying cause.

faqs.question: What if I have multiple decline reasons?
faqs.answer: Address each reason in your appeal with separate evidence for each. Upload multiple documents labeled clearly.
